paper_summary: The paper compares supervised feedforward networks (a standard ANN and an ANN trained with a reward-based loss) with Deep Q-Network (DQN) classifiers for bearing fault diagnosis on the University of Ottawa UORED vibration dataset, split 80/20 into training and test data. Every model is trained on two input representations: 1000-point raw-signal windows with 50% overlap, and vectors of statistical features such as mean, RMS and kurtosis. On raw windows the standard DQN reaches only 33.06% accuracy after close to 11 hours of training, while a timestep-based DQN with a replay buffer reaches 62.57%, near the ANN's 67.45%. On statistical features the DQN reaches 73.33% against 70.00% for the ANN, and 78.33% with a reward matrix tuned by trial and error. The paper does not report repeated runs, seeds, hardware or code.

method_overview.overview: Four model types are compared: a standard feedforward ANN, an ANN with a reward-based loss, a DQN, and an alternative DQN trained over timesteps with a replay buffer. The networks share the architecture of Table II (fully connected input layer to 128 units, a 128-unit hidden layer, an output layer over the classes), except the alternative DQN, which the paper says has a different architecture. Inputs are either raw vibration windows of 1000 points with 50% overlap or statistical feature vectors. Models 1-4 use windows and models 5-8 use feature vectors; model 8 adds a hand-designed reward matrix.

suggested_experiments.title: Recording-level split
suggested_experiments.goal: Check whether overlapping windows leak between training and test data.
steps: Split UORED by recording or bearing so that no recording contributes windows to both sets.
Retrain models 1-4 on windows and compare accuracy with Table V.

suggested_experiments.title: Seeds and variance
suggested_experiments.goal: Find out whether the 4% and 8% DQN gains exceed run-to-run noise.
steps: Train models 5-8 with five seeds each.
Report mean and standard deviation of accuracy and F1, and a significance test for DQN against ANN.

suggested_experiments.title: Reward matrix against class weights
suggested_experiments.goal: Test whether the tailored reward helps beyond what a class-weighted supervised loss gives.
steps: Hold out a validation split and tune the reward matrix and ANN class weights on it.
Compare model 8 with an ANN trained with the tuned class weights on the untouched test split.

suggested_experiments.title: Cross-domain test
suggested_experiments.goal: Measure the adaptability the paper attributes to RL.
steps: Train on one UORED operating condition or bearing and test on another.
Compare the drop in accuracy for the ANN and the DQN.
